analysis: Both changed files are Swift test files. FlintAnswerStopTests.swift adds one line (head line 130) to FlintStreamOutcome.record: `case .logprobs: break`. FlintResponseFormatTests.swift line 362 changes `case .info: break` to `case .info, .logprobs: break`. These are only exhaustive-switch updates in test helpers, apparently needed because MLXServerGenerationEvent gained a `.logprobs` case in a source change that is not in this batch. Neither edit touches production code, keys, attestation, authorization, cache storage or coordinator wire handling. Neither adds attack surface, so no regression is attributable to this diff. The test suites exercise the Flint native constraint, answer-stop filtering, response_format validation (no content quoted in errors) and the scheduler/bridge path. They confirm stop text inside reasoning or tool arguments is not matched, and that other model families keep engine stop strings. Unverified, outside the supplied evidence: the production source that introduces `.logprobs`. That change deserves review for A-001 prompt/completion exposure, for example whether logprobs are emitted to consumers, whether they leak tokens that were stripped or held back by the stop filter or reasoning handling, and whether they are encrypted in transit under TB-002/T-008. The tests silently ignore `.logprobs`, so they provide no coverage for those behaviors. Related threats T-007, T-008 and T-041 (retained cache threat) are not affected by this PR's test-only lines.
